conservationStatus.scope: 2025 regional Red List for South Africa, Eswatini and Lesotho. Wikipedia reports a global IUCN assessment (2017) of Least Concern.

sources.title: Roan Antelope
sources.note: 2025 regional assessment: Vulnerable (downlisted from Endangered); regional trend declining. Kruger subpopulation described as having stabilised after a 1986–1993 crash.

sources.title: Roan antelope
sources.note: Speciesbox cites a 2017 IUCN SSC Antelope Specialist Group assessment of Least Concern.

size.note: Structured shoulder height (135–160 cm) and head-and-body length (typically 235–285 cm) follow the Kingdon et al. (2013) figures quoted in Wikipedia's description; that account also gives an unsplit mass of 230–320 kg and a tail of up to 54 cm. Wikipedia's lead, citing other sources, disagrees: shoulder height around 130–140 cm, head-and-body length 190–240 cm, tail 37–48 cm, males 242–300 kg and females 223–280 kg. The sex-split mass and the tail range used here follow that lead. Animal Diversity Web gives males 150–160 cm and females 140–160 cm at the shoulder, and males 260–300 kg and females 225–275 kg. These disagreements are recorded, not averaged. Horns reach up to 100 cm in males and are slightly shorter in females.

summary: A large, horse-like antelope of wooded savanna, with a roan or grey-brown coat, a dark face mask, long tufted ears, and ringed, backswept horns in both sexes. It is one of Kruger's scarcest antelope, reduced to a small subpopulation after a sharp decline in the late twentieth century. The official English name on the 2011 checklist is Roan.
description: The coat is roan to grey-brown or amber, often with a reddish tinge, and the underparts are paler, yellow to white. The face is dark, with a black mask around the eyes and on the bridge of the snout and white patches around the eyes and the mouth; the mask is described as somewhat lighter in females. The ears are long, narrow and donkey-like, with dark-brown tufts 3–5 cm long at the tips. A short, erect mane runs from the back of the neck to the withers, and a light shaggy neckbeard is more pronounced in males. The legs are darker than the body, and the tail is dark with a black tuft. Both sexes have ringed, scimitar-shaped horns that arch backward, up to 100 cm in males and slightly shorter in females. Young animals are much lighter and reddish-brown. The official checklist name is Roan; iNaturalist prefers Roan Antelope.
habits: Lives in small harem herds, typically of about 5 to 15 animals (sometimes up to 35), with one dominant male and a hierarchy among the females. Males fight on their knees with their horns. Animals are mainly active in the cooler morning and evening hours and rest in thicker cover in the heat of the day. Young males are forced out of the herd at about three years and may form small bachelor groups. In Kruger the species is scarce: one source describes a 90% crash in the park's largest subpopulation between 1986 and 1993, after which the subpopulation is said to have stabilised at a low total.

diet.summary: A grazer of mid-length grasses that prefers leaves over stems and will browse if grazing is poor. Animal Diversity Web gives a preferred feeding height of 15–150 cm, and notes that animals feed in the morning and evening and retreat to more densely wooded areas in the middle of the day.

young: A single calf is born after a gestation of 260 to 281 days. Sources describe breeding as possible throughout the year, with no distinct season. The female leaves the herd about one or two weeks before giving birth and hides the newborn for about four or five weeks, returning to it at dusk, until the calf is strong enough to join the herd. Young animals are much lighter and reddish-brown. Exact calving months for Kruger were not found.
habitat: Lightly wooded savanna, woodland and grassland with medium to tall grass, and access to water. Photographs in this file come from the north of Kruger National Park, the Mopani area, and eastern Kruger north of Olifants.

similar.note: Roan is paler (roan or grey-brown) and heavier, with shorter, less backswept horns, long tufted ears, and a dark face with white patches. Sable is darker, with a white belly, a strongly contrasted black-and-white face, and longer, more arched scimitar horns. Adult male sable are almost black.

population.notes: One source claims a current Kruger total of 58 roan (35–41 mature individuals), after a 90% crash in the park's largest subpopulation between 1986 and 1993 and a reported total of 50 in 2012, and describes the Kruger subpopulation as having since stabilised. A more accurate figure may be available at this URL: https://www.sanparks.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/KNP-wildlife-trends.pdf Regional Red List status is Vulnerable, with a declining national trend.

viewNotes.note: A roan or grey-brown coat, a dark face with white patches, long tufted ears, a short erect mane, darker legs and backswept horns.
The black face mask, white patches around the eyes and mouth, and long, spread, tufted ears are clearest from the front.
A paler body than a large adult, a rufous mane, and shorter, still-developing horns.
